idiom_name: abstract record base + sealed record variants + switch expression
implementation_notes: Records supply the product half (positional parameters, value equality, with-expressions for non-destructive copies) and switch expressions with positional/property patterns supply the eliminator, which deconstructs payloads directly in the case labels. The compiler treats the switch as exhaustive once the base is a closed hierarchy - the C# 15 'closed' modifier makes the direct descendants a compile-time known set - so before C# 15 a discard arm is required even though sealed descendants make it unreachable. Use this form on the LTS toolchains; recursive records model trees.
pitfalls: Before C# 15 the compiler cannot prove exhaustiveness for a hierarchy, so a discard arm is mandatory and can silently absorb a new variant - prefer declaring the base 'closed' when the compiler supports it.
Pattern matching on a base type that is not sealed lets any assembly add a subtype, so the union is only as closed as your declarations.
Switch expressions throw SwitchExpressionException at run time when no arm matches; a discard arm that returns default turns that error into silent misbehaviour.
Positional patterns depend on the record's primary constructor order, so reordering parameters silently changes every deconstruction site.

variants.name: Closed record class + exhaustive switch (C# 15)
variants.implementation_notes: C# 15's closed modifier makes a record class hierarchy closed to direct descendants outside its declaring assembly; records still provide value-like products and switch patterns are exhaustive over all direct descendants. The base is implicitly abstract, direct children must be declared in the same assembly and module, and nullable selectors still require a null arm. Use this when all variants ship in one assembly; use a plain interface or open base when extension is intentional.
pitfalls: A closed base only closes direct descendants; an unsealed child can still be subclassed elsewhere -> mark each child sealed or closed when the whole tree must remain closed.
A Shape? selector has an extra null case; omitting null leaves the switch non-exhaustive -> handle null or keep the selector non-null.
Closed classes constrain the hierarchy to one declaring assembly; use an interface or open base when plugins must add variants.
